question: Polyatomic positive ions often have common names ending with the suffix ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**-onium.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **-onium:-**

 
 
• It​ is a common suffix for** polyatomic positive ions. **
 
• The "-onium" suffix is used to indicate that a** cation** is composed of** two or more atoms, **such as **ammonium (NH4+) or phosphonium (PH4+)**. 
 
• This naming convention is useful for** identifying and communicating** the composition and charge of **polyatomic ions** in chemical reactions and other contexts. ​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polyatomic ions:-**

 
 
• These​ are ions that consist of **two or more atoms** that are **covalently bonded **or have a **net positive or negative charge.** 
 
• Common examples of** polyatomic positive ions** include **ammonium (NH4+), hydronium (H3O+), and methylammonium (CH3NH3+)**. 
 
 
 
• **"-ium"** :-
 
 
• It is often added to the end of the name of a** polyatomic positive ion** to indicate that it is a **cation (positively charged ion).** 
 
 
 
• **"-ic" :-**
 
 
• **​**It** **is commonly used to indicate the** presence of an acid**, while **"-ous" **is used to indicate a **lower oxidation state** of an element. 
 
 
 
• **"-ide":-**
 
 
• It​ is typically used to indicate an** anion **(negatively charged ion), such as **chloride (Cl-) or oxide (O2-). **
